symptoms: Dull olive-green patches appear on young leaves.
Underside spots turn dark brown to black and feel velvety.
Leaves may curl, twist and turn yellow early.
Fruit gets small, rough, black round spots, often at the flower end.
Young fruit spots can have a yellow ring.
entries.look_alikes: Black rot leaf spots have a purple edge and tan centre (frogeye). Cedar apple rust spots are yellow-orange and swollen.
cultural_actions: Follow university and horticulture department spray schedules.
entries.when_to_act: Himachal advisory: follow the spray schedule from the university and horticulture department. Disease favours cool, moist early spring.

ask_back.question: Are the spots olive-green to dark brown, velvety, on the leaf underside?
Are the leaf spots yellow-orange, swollen, with a red border?
Do leaf spots have a purple edge with a tan-brown centre?

entries.caveats: Symptoms and cleaning advice from TNAU (general); fungicide names from a news report of a Himachal university advisory and a journal abstract, not label pages. In India apple is grown in Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Arunachal Pradesh; check local advice.

entries.name_en: Black rot and frogeye leaf spot
symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves grow into round spots.
Spot edge stays purple while the centre turns brown or tan (frogeye).
Fruit rots at the flower end, usually one spot per fruit.
Rotten patch is firm and leathery with dark and light bands.
Rotten fruit dries into a hard mummy; limbs get sunken reddish-brown cankers.
entries.look_alikes: Bitter rot usually has many spots per fruit. Scab leaf spots are olive-green and velvety, without a purple edge.
cultural_actions: Remove cankers, dead wood and mummified fruit.
Cut out cankers well below the diseased edge.

ask_back.question: Do leaf spots have a purple edge and brown or tan centre?
Is the fruit rot at the flower end, usually one spot per fruit?
Are leaf spots olive-green and velvety underneath?

TNAU Agritech - Organic farming: diseases of apple

entries.caveats: Source is a US extension page; no Indian source found. Spray timing not given there. In India apple is grown in Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Arunachal Pradesh; check local advice. Whether this disease is common in India is not confirmed by the sources.

entries.cause: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae (fungus, needs juniper or cedar)
symptoms: Tiny yellow spots appear on leaves in spring.
Spots grow, turn yellow-orange and swell, with a red border.
Black dots show in the centre of the spots.
Fruit and twigs of susceptible varieties can also be hit.
entries.look_alikes: Scab spots are olive-green to black and velvety, not swollen and yellow-orange.
cultural_actions: Remove galls from nearby juniper before spore horns form.
Ask local extension or garden centre about fungicide options.
entries.when_to_act: Source: wet spring weather gives severe infection; removing juniper galls early stops spore release.

ask_back.question: Are the leaf spots yellow-orange, swollen, with a red border and black dots?
Are juniper or cedar trees growing near the orchard?
Are the leaf spots olive-green and velvety underneath?

entries.caveats: US source only. The disease needs juniper or cedar hosts, which may be absent in Indian apple areas, so a match here is less likely; confirm with the local horticulture officer. In India apple is grown in Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Arunachal Pradesh; check local advice. No chemicals named on the page.

symptoms: Leaves are free of olive-green, velvety patches.
No purple-edged frogeye spots on leaves.
No yellow-orange swollen spots on leaves.
Fruit has no rough black spots or rotten patches.
cultural_actions: Remove mummified fruit and dead wood.
Handle fruit carefully to avoid wounds.

symptoms: Irregular reddish-brown spots appear on leaves.
Berries get a black scab and shrivel.
Dark sunken spots can appear on stems and tendrils.
entries.look_alikes: Leaf blight (Isariopsis) on clusters looks like black rot, but the whole cluster collapses, not single berries.
cultural_actions: Keep good air flow in the vine canopy.
entries.when_to_act: NHB: protective sprays on young bunches. Warm, humid, rainy and cloudy weather favours the disease.

ask_back.question: Are berries turning black and hard, with reddish-brown leaf spots?
Does the whole bunch collapse rather than single berries?

entries.caveats: NHB page is a national horticulture board note, not a state or ICAR page. A separate post-harvest black rot caused by Aspergillus niger exists; this entry is the field disease. Check local advice.

entries.cause: Fungal complex including Phaeoacremonium and Phaeomoniella chlamydospora
symptoms: Stripes appear between leaf veins, dark red or yellow.
Striped leaf areas dry out and die.
Berries get small dark spots with brown-purple borders.
Affected berries may crack, dry or spoil.
Cut wood shows rings of dark spots.
entries.look_alikes: Esca belongs to the trunk disease group with Botryosphaeria, Eutypa and Phomopsis dieback.
cultural_actions: Do not rely on sprays: wood infection cannot be cleared by fungicide.
Know that pruning wounds are where infection enters.
Ask a grape specialist about pruning-wound care.
entries.when_to_act: Source: infection enters pruning wounds during rainy periods from fall to spring.

ask_back.question: Do leaves show stripes between veins that turn red or yellow, then dry?
Do berries have small dark spots with purple-brown borders?

No red or yellow stripes between leaf veins.
Berries are free of black scab and dark spots.
Bunches are intact, not collapsing.
cultural_actions: Keep good air flow in the canopy.

symptoms: Irregular spots appear on leaves, dull red to brown at first.
Spots darken as they age.
In bad attacks, spots join together.
On bunches it looks like black rot, but the whole cluster collapses.
It usually shows late in the growing season.
entries.look_alikes: Black rot damages single berries and has reddish-brown leaf spots; here the whole cluster collapses.
cultural_actions: Sprays used for other grape diseases may also reduce this disease.
entries.when_to_act: Source gives no threshold. It appears late in the season; sprays for other diseases may help.

ask_back.question: Does the whole bunch collapse together?
Are single berries turning black and hard instead?

symptoms: Brown-black dead spots appear on leaves.
Spots are angular or oval with rings inside, like a target.
Spots join and spread over the whole leaf.
entries.look_alikes: Late blight spots are water-soaked, turn purple-brown to black, with white growth underneath.
cultural_actions: Remove infected plant debris; spores in soil start infection.
Try Kufri Sindhuri, which has fair resistance.
entries.when_to_act: TNAU: spray very early, then repeat as the label advises. Favoured by dry warm weather with some rain.

ask_back.question: Are the spots brown-black with rings inside, like a target?
Are spots water-soaked with white growth under the leaf?

symptoms: Water-soaked spots appear on leaves and grow larger.
Spots turn purple-brown, then black.
White growth appears on the underside of leaves.
Stems get affected, often at nodes, and plants topple.
Tubers get purplish-brown spots with rusty brown rot inside.
entries.look_alikes: Early blight spots are brown-black with rings inside and no white growth underneath.
cultural_actions: Remove infected tubers and cull piles near storage.
Avoid injuries at harvest; remove visibly infected tubers before storage.
Plant earlier, use wider spacing and hill properly.
Choose resistant varieties such as Kufri Jyoti or Kufri Jeevan.
entries.when_to_act: PAU: start protective sprays before symptoms show. TNAU: protective sprays prevent tuber infection.

ask_back.question: Are leaf spots water-soaked, turning purple-brown, with white growth underneath?
Are the spots brown-black with rings inside, like a target?

Avoid injuries at harvest and check tubers carefully.

symptoms: Small round or irregular spots appear on leaves, dark brown or black and greasy.
Spot centre turns lighter, with a dark edge.
Badly hit leaves turn yellow and fall.
Stems may get cankers and branches wilt.
Fruit gets raised, water-soaked spots with a pale yellow border.
cultural_actions: Work crop residue into soil after harvest.
Rotate away from tomato, chilli and other related crops.
entries.when_to_act: TNAU: avoid antibiotic sprays once fruit development has begun.
